cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: I Told You Enough
cards.instruction: Agree to be honest while repeatedly narrowing what honesty requires and which details count.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. I'll be honest about your missing donation box. You asked where I went; I said the bank.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Did you take the box there?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Yes. You didn't ask what was inside.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Was the money still in it when you arrived?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: At the car park, yes. If you mean the counter, that's a different arrival.

mechanism: A claims authority to define each question so promised honesty covers progressively smaller pieces of the missing-money story.
confusable: Unlike refusing to answer, A gives literal answers while narrowing object contents and location meanings.
comparison: Donation-box arrival at car park versus counter differs from defining dinner and eating in a photograph.
seedUse: The seed already polices what counts as asked and what counts as arrival; S01 reinforces the right A claims to rule on those definitions.
